Liber synodalis of Papiniano della Rovere, Bishop of Novara – issued in 1298 (following celebration of a synod), two years into his episcopate (p36); he had been born in Turin, and was later named bishop of Parma in 1300

-Papiniano was himself closely tied to papacy, having served as a chaplain and “uditore del Palazzo apostolico” [p41] at the request of Boniface VIII [Registres de Boniface VIII, I, n. 914, coll 319-20]

-Novara was under jurisdiction of Milan, but the work shows few traces of the council held at Milan in 1291 [pp. 36-37]

-work is strongly influenced by Guillaume Durand’s statutes (p. 67); follows structure of instructiones et monitiones and then constitutiones (this seems to have been the southern French model, as opposed to Odo of Sully’s, which was pervasive in the North; see Guizard, l’Oeuvre canonique de Guillaume Durand, in XXXIXme Congrès Mende 1955, Montpellier 1955)

-shows itself to be strongly inspired by Bonifician conception of centralized authority [p82]

-Helmrath, Partikularsynoden, 160: 1298 Novara Diocesan Statutes (issued by Bishop Papinianus della Rovere) contained material from Gratian, the Liber Extra, the Synodalbook of William Durandus, the 1252 Statutes of Nimes, a Cologne Synod, the joint 1289 statutes of Cahors, Rodez and Tulle, and other statutes of Novara itself from 1257 and 1277. (cites Briacca, Statuti sinodali, 169-279)

Liber synodalis of Papiniano della Rovere, Bishop of Novara – issued in 1298 (following celebration of a synod), two years into his episcopate (p36); he had been born in Turin, and was later named bishop of Parma in 1300

-Papiniano was himself closely tied to papacy, having served as a chaplain and “uditore del Palazzo apostolico” [p41] at the request of Boniface VIII [Registres de Boniface VIII, I, n. 914, coll 319-20]

-Novara was under jurisdiction of Milan, but the work shows few traces of the council held at Milan in 1291 [pp. 36-37]

-work is strongly influenced by Guillaume Durand’s statutes (p. 67); follows structure of instructiones et monitiones and then constitutiones (this seems to have been the southern French model, as opposed to Odo of Sully’s, which was pervasive in the North; see Guizard, l’Oeuvre canonique de Guillaume Durand, in XXXIXme Congrès Mende 1955, Montpellier 1955)

-shows itself to be strongly inspired by Bonifician conception of centralized authority [p82]

-Helmrath, Partikularsynoden, 160: 1298 Novara Diocesan Statutes (issued by Bishop Papinianus della Rovere) contained material from Gratian, the Liber Extra, the Synodalbook of William Durandus, the 1252 Statutes of Nimes, a Cologne Synod, the joint 1289 statutes of Cahors, Rodez and Tulle, and other statutes of Novara itself from 1257 and 1277. (cites Briacca, Statuti sinodali, 169-279)
BiblioRefs: Briacca, Papiniano della Rovere, Contributi ad una biografia, in Raccolta di Studi in memoria di Giovanni Soranzo, I, Milan 1968, pp60-128, at pp113-14

• à la fin du fol. 68v, figure une note marginale indiquant que la suite du texte ne se trouvait pas dans le ms. de Picard. Suivent :

3) mention d’une publication, par l’évêque Guillaume de Malestroit, présent au synode du jeudi suivant la pentecôte 1444, des statuts de Jean et Henri
4) mention du sceau apposé sur le texte par les vicaires de Guillaume de Malestroit, alors absent du diocèse, le 17 juin 1445.
